messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding gpt-2-8b (8-bit quant) on A100 fleet. Same SKU + driver reported on AWS/GCP/Azure but seeing a consistent perf inversion: Azure p95 >> GCP. Anyone seen this kind of "perf flip" across providers?

aj: Can you paste the driver/CUDA versions + MIG config? also the small benchmark you ran :eyes:

maria: sure, pasted from the canary image:
```
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,gpu_bus_id --format=csv
name, driver_version, pci.bus
NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, 535.86, 0000:3b:00.0

$ cat /usr/local/cuda/version.txt
CUDA Version 12.2

$ uname -a
Linux az-canary-01 5.15.0-70-generic #77-Ubuntu SMP x86_64 GNU/Linux
```

sam: ran a tiny throughput/latency microbench across regions (same binary, same seed). numbers below (p95 in ms):
```
region,p95_ms,throughput_tokens_s
aws-us-west-2,34,8200
gcp-us-west1,33,8350
az-west,42,7600
```
az is ~25% worse at p95, throughput down ~8%.

perf-bot: automated-run-2071234567: nvml reports >6% PCIe stall cycles on az-west instances during the run. See logs: https://internal.perf/logs/2071234567 (attached) :robot_face:

aj: interesting — common culprits: kernel differences, PCIe ASPM, BIOS power/perf governors, NUMA/CPU pinning, driver microcode. did you check cuBLAS/alg selection fallbacks?

maria: I grepped runtime logs and saw this repeated line during the slower runs:
```
W cublasLt: algo selection fallback for int8 gemm, heuristic failed, trying fallback path
```

ops-elaine: FYI Azure images we spun up used kernel 5.15 and had default CPU governor "ondemand" plus ASML PCIe settings. GCP base image was 5.19 with performance governor in our prebuilt. BIOS firmware rev differs by ~1 on the vendor side (we have a ticket open).

sam: reran on az with kernel upgraded to 5.19 and governor set to "performance":
```
region,p95_ms,throughput_tokens_s
az-west-5.19,36,8000
```
still ~9% worse than GCP but much closer — suggests multi-factor causes.

aj: next experiments I'd run (short list):
1) nvprof / ncu traces for kernel launch latency + memcopy times
2) microbench memcpy bw across PCIe root complexes (host->device / device->host)
3) force cuBLAS deterministic algorithm or preselect algo to avoid fallbacks
4) check IRQ affinity / rps settings on the NICs

maria: I'll kick off (1) and (2) across a 3-node canary in parallel and dump perf counters. also trying CUDA 11.8 image to see if cublas behavior changes.

perf-bot: queued ncu jobs: jobids 98321..98323 across aws/gcp/az - will annotate with kernel-level stalls and sm_active_percent.

aj: if the ncu shows memcpy or PCIe stall hotspots, try setting `pci=realloc=on` kernel param and toggle ACS overrides (careful with security). also check if nv_peer_memory is loaded differently on azure.

maria: noted. I'll update the onboarding checklist / infra playbook with a troubleshooting section for "provider parity gap" — steps to run before flagging model as "ready".

sam: one more thing — saw a single host on az with lower fan/profile settings; thermal throttling was false but clocks were ~50 MHz lower under sustained load. might explain residual gap.

maria: great — thanks all. scheduling a 2pm canary run tomorrow and will paste the compact CSV + NCU highlights here. :calendar:
